# grith documentation

grith is a security-first local AI agent platform. It intercepts every
syscall an AI agent makes, scores it through 18 filters, and routes
ambiguous calls to a human-review queue.

These docs describe grith v0.3.1, the current release. It runs on Linux
x86_64 and aarch64; there is no macOS or Windows build. Every page describes
behaviour that ships today - the one exception is marked [coming soon].

Site: https://docs.grith.ai

## Sections

### Start here

- [What is grith](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/start/what-is-grith) — An OS-level security supervisor for AI agents: intercept every action, score it against 18 filters, hold the ambiguous ones for a human.
- [Installation](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/start/installation) — One line to install grith on Linux, what the installer verifies before it writes anything, and where the files land.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/start/quickstart) — Four commands: create a config, run your agent under grith, answer a prompt, read the audit log.
- [Choose your agent](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/start/choose-your-agent) — grith picks a supervisor profile from the command name. Here is the table it uses, the eleven built-in profiles, and what a profile changes.
- [Connect a model](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/start/connect-a-model) — Provider setup for grith run and the built-in REPL. Not needed if you only supervise other agents with grith exec.
- [Reviewing the digest](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/start/reviewing-the-digest) — Where a held call shows up, every key that decides it, and what happens when nobody answers.

### Concepts

- [The threat model](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/concepts/threat-model) — The attacker grith is built for, the attackers it is not, and where the trust boundary sits.
- [Syscall interception](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/concepts/syscall-interception) — seccomp-BPF picks the syscalls worth stopping, ptrace stops them, and grith answers before the kernel acts.
- [The three-phase pipeline](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/concepts/three-phase-pipeline) — Eighteen filters in three phases, parallel within a phase, with a deny in an early phase ending the evaluation there.
- [Composite scoring](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/concepts/composite-scoring) — The composite is a plain sum of what matched, and two strict comparisons decide allow, queue or deny.
- [The quarantine digest](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/concepts/quarantine-digest) — What happens to a call that scores between 3.0 and 8.0, who answers it, and what happens if nobody does.
- [The daemon and thin-client sessions](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/concepts/daemon-and-sessions) — One process owns the audit log, the filters and the queue; every supervised session is a client of it over loopback HTTP.
- [The workspace boundary](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/concepts/workspace-boundary) — Two subtractive controls - a session-wide filesystem fence and a per-directory block - that refuse without prompting.
- [Session containment](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/concepts/session-containment) — Two different mechanisms share the name: a sticky session-lifetime lock armed by high taint, and a 600-second scoring window.
- [Taint tracking](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/concepts/taint-tracking) — What counts as a sensitive source, which of the three levels it gets, and what the two data-flow defaults changed.
- [Adaptive reputation](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/concepts/adaptive-reputation) — The learned trust table: what it observes, where it is applied, and why it only ever flips a queue to an allow.
- [Canary tokens](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/concepts/canary-tokens) — Decoy secrets that deny outbound calls at 9.5 - and the persistence gap you have to work around to register one.

### CLI reference

- [CLI overview](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/overview) — Every top-level grith command, the five global flags, and the two aliases that are not in --help.
- [grith run](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/run) — Run one task through the built-in agent, or drop into the REPL by running grith with no arguments.
- [grith exec](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/exec) — Supervise an external CLI tool at the syscall level - flags, session verbs, prompt keys and the daemon requirement.
- [grith proxy test](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/proxy-test) — Dry-run a tool call through all 18 filters and see the decision, the score and every contribution.
- [grith digest](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/digest) — List the quarantine queue, and review held calls one keypress at a time.
- [grith audit](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/audit) — Read, verify, export and maintain the hash-chained audit log of every decision grith made.
- [grith log](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/log) — A readable feed of decisions, historic or live, filtered to one session.
- [grith canary](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/canary) — Register decoy credentials the exfiltration filter watches for - and the persistence gap you must know about.
- [grith supervisor](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/supervisor) — List active supervised sessions, inspect one in detail, or terminate it.
- [grith daemon](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/daemon) — Start, stop and check the daemon that owns the audit database, the digest queue and the dashboard - and authorise a browser.
- [grith profile audit](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/profile-audit) — Replay a recorded syscall trace against a profile to see what it missed and what it never used.
- [grith reputation](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/reputation) — Inspect or reset the trust table grith learns from your approve and deny decisions.
- [grith notifications](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/notifications) — What the command does today: prints a status message and exits.
- [grith config](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/config) — Print the effective configuration, or set one key from a fixed 58-key whitelist.
- [grith init](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/init) — Write a default config.toml. It overwrites any file already there, with no backup and no merge.
- [grith setup](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/setup) — The interactive first-run wizard: pick how you will use grith, connect a provider, start a trial.
- [grith pro](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/pro) — Sign in, activate and refresh a licence, pull team policy, and manage billing from the terminal.
- [grith analytics](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/analytics) — Check, consent to or turn off cloud analytics sync, and verify that archived days still match the dashboard.
- [grith completions](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/cli/completions) — Print a shell completion script to stdout. Works even when your config is broken.

### Filter reference

- [Filter overview](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/overview) — The 18 filters grith runs on every supervised call, in the order they run, and what each one can add to the score.
- [1. Operation risk scoring](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/01-operation-risk-scoring) — The baseline every call starts from, decided purely by what kind of operation it is.
- [2. Static path matching](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/02-static-path-matching) — Fifteen anchored path rules from paths.toml - the curated list of files that are always worth a decision.
- [3. Sensitive path heuristic](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/03-sensitive-path-heuristic) — Built-in heuristics for credential-shaped paths the curated list does not name.
- [4. Allowlist / denylist](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/04-allowlist-denylist) — Your own allow and deny patterns - the one filter that can pull the composite down.
- [5. Argument length & structure](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/05-argument-length-structure) — Oversized arguments, shell metacharacters in a path, and deep traversal.
- [6. Capability enforcement](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/06-capability-enforcement) — Grant a caller a set of operation classes, and everything outside them scores 10.0.
- [7. Secret / credential scanning](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/07-secret-credential-scanning) — 1617 credential patterns, matched against the arguments of every call in a single pass.
- [8. Command structure analysis](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/08-command-structure-analysis) — Twelve shell-shape rules, with carveouts so routine invocations of sudo and systemctl do not queue.
- [9. Destructive action](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/09-destructive-action) — Formats, wipes, drops and teardowns - hard-denied when catastrophic, escalated when they target production.
- [10. Egress policy](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/10-egress-policy) — Where a call is going, on what port, over what scheme - and whether the payload is shaped like exfiltration.
- [11. DLP gate](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/11-dlp-gate) — Eleven high-confidence secret patterns on outbound calls only, banded by a single policy setting.
- [12. Canary detection](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/12-canary-detection) — Values you planted yourself, scored at 9.5 - above the deny line, on purpose.
- [13. Destination reputation](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/13-destination-reputation) — A fixed domain list plus two shape checks - not the learned trust table.
- [14. Behavioural anomaly](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/14-behavioural-anomaly) — How unusual an authority-changing call is against the baseline this session has built.
- [15. Taint tracking](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/15-taint-tracking) — Sensitive data read earlier in the session, correlated with the call that could send it out.
- [16. Session containment](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/16-session-containment) — A 600-second window after a sensitive read, during which anything outbound costs more.
- [17. Rate limiting](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/17-rate-limiting) — Per-category call volume, gated so that only risk-bearing operations can escalate.
- [18. Egress rate](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/18-egress-rate) — Outbound volume, destination spread and the read-then-send shape, per session.
- [Meta-rules](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/filters/meta-rules) — Five rules that adjust the composite once, after phase 3, when a specific combination of filters fired.

### Configuration

- [Configuration overview](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/config/overview) — The five config layers, the sparse-file trap that bricks the CLI, and how to write config safely.
- [[general]](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/config/general) — Log level, audit directory, and the three toggles that decide what grith talks to grith.ai about.
- [[audit]](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/config/audit) — How much of a session is recorded, how long it stays in the active database, and where the rest goes.
- [[proxy]](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/config/proxy) — Scoring thresholds, the filter switches, and the four behavioural knobs that change what fires.
- [[reputation]](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/config/reputation) — Tunables for the learned trust table - the thing that can flip a queued call to allow after enough clean history.
- [[supervisor]](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/config/supervisor) — Session limits, the seven syscall-coverage flags, how far workspace trust reaches, and DNS inspection.
- [[server]](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/config/server) — The local HTTP API and dashboard - bind address, native TLS, idle shutdown and the four rate-limit buckets.
- [[llm]](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/config/llm) — Provider and model for grith run and the REPL, and the three places an API key can come from.
- [Filter config files](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/config/filter-config-files) — The ten TOML files filters load, where an override has to sit, and why an override replaces rather than extends.
- [Environment variables](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/config/environment-variables) — Every GRITH_ variable grith reads, what it overrides, and the boolean spelling that silently does nothing.

### Supervisor profiles

- [How profiles work](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/profiles/how-profiles-work) — What a supervisor profile trusts, how grith picks one for a session, and why you cannot write your own.
- [Built-in profiles](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/profiles/built-in-profiles) — The 11 profiles compiled into grith, what each one trusts, and how a session gets one.

### API reference

- [API overview](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/api/overview) — Where the daemon binds, how each route is authorised, the rate-limit buckets, and what an error body looks like.
- [Authentication](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/api/authentication) — The three secrets the daemon holds, how a browser gets its token, and which guard rejects you with which status.
- [Health and tier](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/api/health-and-tier) — Liveness, plan tier, licence refresh state and the narrow config read/write the dashboard uses.
- [Proxy](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/api/proxy) — Filter pipeline state, and a dry-run endpoint that scores a tool call without executing anything.
- [Digest](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/api/digest) — Read the quarantine queue and resolve items over REST, including the nonce-authenticated review callback.
- [Audit](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/api/audit) — Page the audit log, aggregate a window, export it, and read the exfiltration rollup.
- [Analytics](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/api/analytics) — The two local analytics-v2 routes, what each tier gets, and the freshness block that tells you how far behind the projection is.
- [Canaries](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/api/canaries) — List, add, rotate and remove canary tokens - and what happens to them when the daemon restarts.
- [Supervisor sessions](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/api/supervisor) — List, inspect, create and terminate supervised sessions, plus the two session-scoped reads that sit outside this prefix.
- [Sync and policies](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/api/sync-and-policies) — What team sync has pulled to this machine, how to apply it, and the local policy store behind the policy editor.
- [Daemon IPC](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/api/ipc) — The bearer-token surface the CLI uses to talk to its own daemon - sessions, audit ingestion, digest items, reputation and events.
- [WebSocket](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/api/websocket) — The two live streams, how the handshake is authorised, and the exact frames the daemon actually emits.

### Guides

- [Tuning scoring thresholds](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/guides/tuning-scoring-thresholds) — Where the allow and deny lines actually fall, how to move them, and when moving them is the wrong fix.
- [Running grith in CI](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/guides/running-in-ci) — Headless sessions fail closed - what gets auto-denied, what --allow-queued changes, and how to unblock a pipeline.
- [Setting up canary tokens](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/guides/setting-up-canary-tokens) — The only registration that survives a restart, what detection actually covers, and how to verify it fires.
- [Containment walkthrough](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/guides/containment-walkthrough) — What changes in a session after it touches something sensitive - the 600-second window, and the sticky flag that never expires.
- [Exfiltration walkthrough](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/guides/exfiltration-walkthrough) — A credential leaving the machine, scored call by call - and the part of it grith never sees.
- [Team setup](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/guides/team-setup) — Getting a team onto grith: what each machine does for itself, what syncs, and what never leaves the developer.
- [TLS and reverse proxies](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/guides/reverse-proxy-tls) — Native TLS for the daemon, and what it takes to reach the dashboard from another machine.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/guides/troubleshooting) — The errors grith actually produces, what each one means, and the fix.

### Security

- [Limitations](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/security/limitations) — What grith cannot see, cannot stop, and does not enforce at shipped defaults.
- [Trust boundaries](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/security/trust-boundaries) — What grith trusts, what it treats as hostile, and which crossing each control sits on.
- [Supervisor-only assessment](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/security/supervisor-only-assessment) — grith enforces on one path. This is what that path carries, what has been closed, and what has not.
- [Security advisories](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/security/advisories) — Where advisories are published, which versions get fixes, and how fast.
- [Responsible disclosure](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/security/responsible-disclosure) — Found a vulnerability in grith? Here's how to report it.

- [Authentication](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/pro/authentication) — Linking a machine to your grith.ai account with browser device auth or an API key, and where the credentials land.
- [Licence lifecycle](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/pro/license-lifecycle) — How the signed licence is verified, refreshed and allowed to lapse, and what happens when the network is gone.
- [Team sync](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/pro/team-sync) — What grith pro sync pulls down, what it pushes up, and what stays on the machine no matter what.
- [Centralised policies](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/pro/centralised-policies) — Authoring a team policy in the dashboard, where it lands on each device, and which team-managed settings actually change a decision.
- [Analytics](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/pro/analytics) — What the local dashboard shows, what syncs to your team, and what never leaves the machine.
- [Encrypted key management](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/pro/encrypted-key-management) — Sharing provider API keys across a team, where they are encrypted, and exactly what that protects against.
- [Notifications](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/pro/notifications) [coming soon] — Review and answer a grith prompt from Telegram, Slack and more, set up from the grith.ai dashboard.

- [Performance and tuning](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/ops/performance-tuning) — What grith actually costs at startup and per syscall, and the handful of settings that change it.
- [Logging and audit retention](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/ops/logging-and-audit-retention) — Where grith writes its logs, what the audit database records, and how long any of it is kept.

- [Verifying releases](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/ops/verifying-releases) — The six files published per target, and the exact commands that prove a grith download is the one CI built.

### Resources

- [Architecture overview](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/resources/architecture-overview) — One daemon owns the audit log, the digest and the filter pipeline; every supervised session is a thin client that fails closed without it.
- [Glossary](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/resources/glossary) — The terms used across these docs, each defined against what v0.3.1 actually does.
- [FAQ](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/resources/faq) — Short answers to the questions people ask before and just after installing grith.
- [Changelog](https://docs.grith.ai/docs/resources/changelog) — What changed in grith v0.3.1, and where to find the releases before it.
